chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Grofe and Bargy shows; first playing vibes
summary: He works commercial shows for Ferde Grofe and Roy Bargy at night and plays NBC's studio vibes with strings.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yes. And then from playing that some of the guys in the Whiteman band came down and then Whiteman was so popular at that time that Ferde Grofé had a show.
Yeah.

And I did his show. And then Roy Bargy had a show and I did his show at night. Besides working in the daytime, I was doing commercial shows at night. I was really working hard, but it was wonderful --
You must've been.
So I was playing -- yeah I was playing vibes and with some of the string sections that -- I'd write vibe parts and xylophone parts and marimba parts --
Well you didn't say anything about having started -- playing vibes --
Huh?
You didn't say that you'd started playing vibes. Well when did --
Well, that's the same -- vibes were new in those days --
Yeah.
In those years, they were just out. Like I told you, they had no pedal, much -- at the -- beginning --
Yeah.
Any mallet-played instruments. I even monkeyed -- tried to play timpanis in those days.
Really? Well I mean, but so -- you went out and bought -- bought yourself vibes?
No, they had one in the studio.
Oh, they had it in the studio.
Yeah.
Yeah.
They had -- NBC had vibes.
Yeah. Yeah, I see.
But they weren't very good ones and usually the drummer -- I forget who the drummer was on the shows, they usually brought a set of vibes, I didn't own one.
Hm. Yeah, yeah.
